title: Machine learning identifies GATA factors coordinating Arabidopsis root development
summary: Single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data were used to reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue, showing a major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone with extensive chromatin remodeling. Machine learning applied to the integrated trajectories identified GATA transcription factors as central coordinators of this switch, a role the authors validated experimentally. The GATA factors sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system integrating auxin and cytokinin inputs. Machine learning is one of several analyses in the study.
ai_technology: Machine learning on integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories

evidence.tested: Experimental validation of the GATA factors' role in the proliferation-to-differentiation switch.
evidence.unknown: How much of the result depends on the machine-learning step versus other analyses; the validation details were not in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning examined integrated trajectories to identify GATA transcription factors as coordinators.
